chapter: Larry in Chicago and New York
title: Joe Frisco and Tom Brown's band
summary: Harry and Russell trace how Joe Frisco heard Brown's band in New Orleans, took them to Chicago, and the band flopped in Chicago and New York.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: He took them to Chicago. Yeah.

First time. And he was, uh, Tom Brown showed us a letter. He had written to Joe, uh, Tom and he had written to Frisco. You know, that's when Nick was trying to say he was the first one to go to Chicago or something. And I think they had a letter from Joe Frisco saying that he hired Tom Brown. Uh huh. On a certain date, you know, they were. That's right.

Trying to show that they. I understand, uh, he was working up here at Farmer, cause it's Ratskiller. That was a restaurant up here. Who, who was that? Tom Brown? No, Joe Frisco was dancing up there then. Uh huh. And he heard the band. They were advertising a prize fight or something. Brown's band. And he liked the band. And he told him that he could place them on a job in Chicago. But they flopped. Whether he worked with the band or not, I don't know. He may have had. He may have booked, uh, the band with him, but they flopped in Chicago.
And they went on to New York as an act. They worked in Broadville. They flopped in New York. Uh, Arnold Loi Canna can tell you all about that. Yeah. He was with the bunch. Yeah.
